name: WF-05 Recovery Execution
description: Onward Phase 6: executes one approved recovery plan -- revalidates freshness, dispatches plan-type-driven real actions (work order, Slack, Calendar, Gmail, reservation, inventory), records each action idempotently, determines overall execution state.
note: Published and live-gate-tested (Phase 6). Execute Workflow Trigger, called by WF-05a with { approval_id }. Freshness: recomputes the state fingerprint via decision-engine's stateless POST /recovery/plan and compares against recovery_runs.state_fingerprint BEFORE touching anything -- a mismatch is refused (audit_log 'execution_refused_stale_plan'), zero execution_runs rows created, proven live with a deliberately-wrong stored fingerprint. Idempotency at the run level: Check Existing Execution + Already Completed? short-circuits a retry of a completed run (execution_actions count unchanged). Idempotency at the action level: Fetch Existing Actions (alwaysOutputData:true -- required, a fresh run legitimately returns 0 rows and without this flag the workflow silently halted here) + Compute Execution Plan precompute which action_types are already 'completed' and the next attempts count per type; each action's own '<X> Already Done?' IF gate skips the real external call when already done. The 12 'Insert <X> Action Success/Failed' nodes are httpRequest PostgREST upserts (POST .../execution_actions?on_conflict=action_key with Prefer: resolution=merge-duplicates,return=representation), not plain Supabase-create inserts -- required because action_key carries a UNIQUE constraint and a retry of a previously-failed action must UPDATE that row (incrementing attempts), not violate the constraint; this was a real defect found and fixed live (23505 duplicate key on retry) before the fix. Plan Type Switch dispatches only the actions relevant to plan_type: repair_via_technician -> work_order + slack_notify only; replace_asset -> + inventory_decrement; relocate_operation -> + resource_reservation + calendar_update + gmail_notify -- proven live with a real relocate_operation execution hitting exactly its 5 expected action types, not a fixed cascade. Real external integrations: Post Slack Message (Slack node, oAuth2, channel #onward-demo in the Onward Demo workspace -- the existing dedicated test channel, per explicit instruction, not a guessed name), Create Calendar Event (googleCalendar node, calendar 'primary'), Send Gmail Notification (gmail node, to the developer's own test address) -- all onError:continueErrorOutput so a real integration failure routes to a distinct branch and is recorded as a 'failed' execution_actions row instead of crashing the workflow. Compute Overall Status (Code node) compares completed_types against plan-type-specific expected_action_types to set execution_runs.status to completed/partially_completed/failed -- proven live via a real Slack failure (fixed, then retried: attempts 1 -> 2, no duplicate row, only the unfinished action re-attempted). Second live-gate pass found and fixed a real defect in all 6 'Insert <X> Action Failed' nodes: the error expression assumed $json.error was always an object with .message (true for httpRequest-style error output), but the native Supabase/Slack/googleCalendar/gmail nodes' onError:continueErrorOutput puts the error as a plain string merged into the passthrough item instead, so the fallback JSON.stringify($json) captured an unrelated upstream item instead of the real error text -- fixed with a typeof check, verified live with a fresh induced resource_reservation FK-violation failure producing a clean error string post-fix. Plan-type dispatch further proven with a real repair_via_technician execution (POS-07) hitting exactly work_order+slack_notify, zero calendar/reservation/gmail rows. Staleness re-proven with a genuine resource mutation (Room 1.01 status flipped to unavailable, not a fabricated fingerprint) causing a real fingerprint mismatch and refusal. Partial-failure + targeted retry re-proven end-to-end on a fresh incident: induced FK-violation failure on resource_reservation only, then a direct retry (via a temporary webhook, removed after) completed only that action (attempts 1->2), leaving all 4 already-completed actions' external references unchanged. Phase 7 finding: a real transient Supabase 504 Gateway Timeout on Fetch Approval crashed an entire execution run with zero trace (no execution_runs row, no audit_log entry) -- CLAUDE.md §14 already mandates retry-on-fail for every external call but no node had it configured. Fixed by adding retryOnFail (3 tries, 1s wait) to every Supabase read/write on the critical path (all Fetch nodes, Insert Execution Run, Update Execution Run Final, Insert Audit Log Final, Insert Audit Log Stale) so a one-off transient failure self-heals instead of silently discarding the run. Phase 7 concurrency test: 3 truly-concurrent invocations of the same approval_id (via a temporary webhook, added/tested/removed) all resolved safely and identically -- in this case all three correctly detected the plan as stale (a real resource mutation had occurred since planning) and refused with matching audit_log entries, zero execution_runs rows, no crashes and no inconsistent state. Hardening checkpoint: Create Calendar Event now targets the dedicated 'Onward Demo' test calendar (74360ce329cc2d264bdbc0725fe40b32dc08ccc4ef5b777496e1d4238ebf8a79@group.calendar.google.com, pre-created by the user) instead of the connected account's primary calendar -- verified live: a real execution's calendar event was independently confirmed present on Onward Demo (GET .../calendars/<demo_id>/events/<event_id> returned the real event) and genuinely absent from primary (GET .../calendars/primary/events/<event_id> returned a real 404). Recompute Fingerprint's URL updated to the current Cloudflare Quick Tunnel after runtime cleanup. Phase 10 (demo build): Send Gmail Notification now sends to both the lecturer (raihamariam19@gmail.com -- confirmed with the user; the originally-given raihamariam19@gmai.com resolves to an unrelated third-party mail domain, not Gmail) and the student (vuquangduypct@gmail.com) test recipients, comma-separated in the same sendTo field. Message rewritten to an old-room/new-room framing using real incident/plan values already in scope. Verified live: the real sent message's To header contains both addresses (fetched via Gmail API, not just trusted from config).
